dedupe_keys.name: us epa waste reduction model warm greenhouse gas energy and economic factors for materials management pathways

description: The Waste Reduction Model is the US Environmental Protection Agency's tool for comparing the climate, energy and economic effects of different ways of managing waste. A user enters the tonnages of materials, such as paper, metals, plastics, food and construction debris, handled under current practice and under an alternative, for example more recycling or composting instead of landfill. The model then applies life-cycle factors for source reduction, recycling, composting, anaerobic digestion, combustion and landfilling. It reports the difference in greenhouse gas emissions, energy use and jobs, wages and taxes. Version 16 is free to download as an Excel workbook together with an openLCA database, with earlier versions and full documentation of the factors available on the same site. Caveats: the factors reflect US conditions and grids, results are high-level comparisons, not facility estimates, and the change log should be read before comparing results from different versions. Coverage is the United States. Simulation uses: comparing waste management scenarios for emissions and costs in capacity and climate planning. Related records: the global waste sector scenarios (data-global-waste-sector-1990-2050) provide a wider emissions context for such comparisons.
